[INBO 2025 — question paper]
34. (2 points) A geneticist was studying the cell cycle in the root tip cells of a plant. She
microscopically observed that 15 cells were in prophase, 7 cells were in prometaphase, 8
cells were in metaphase, 7 were in anaphase, 5 were in telophase and 88 were in interphase.
The overall cell cycle for this particular species was recorded to be 23 hours. The time span
that the cells are in the mitotic phase is:
Note that the final answer for the question will be given marks only if calculations are shown
in the box given and the final answer is filled in the blank.

[CBSE Class XII Biology, marking scheme, 2025-26]

What happens to chromosomes during anaphase?
Which of the following is a key feature of metaphase in mitosis?
If a cell is observed to have chromosomes aligned at the metaphase plate, which phase of mitosis is it in?

In a plant root tip cell, 15 cells were in prophase, 7 in prometaphase, 8 in metaphase, 7 in anaphase, 5 in telophase, and 88 in interphase. The total cell cycle time is 23 hours. What is the time spent in the mitotic phase?
Based on the passage, which of the following best describes the role of kinetochores during metaphase?
Based on the passage, which of the following is a key difference between meiosis I and meiosis II?
According to the passage, what is the main reason meiosis is important for sexually reproducing organisms?
Which phase of the cell cycle is characterised by the alignment of chromosomes at the equatorial plate?

A geneticist observed 15 cells in prophase, 7 in prometaphase, 8 in metaphase, 7 in anaphase, 5 in telophase, and 88 in interphase. The total cell cycle was 23 hours. What is the time spent in the mitotic phase?

A student observed 150 cells in a sample of root tip tissue. Out of these, 30 cells were in prophase, 10 in metaphase, 5 in anaphase, and 5 in telophase. The total cell cycle time was recorded as 12 hours. What is the approximate time spent by the cells in mitosis?
Which phase of meiosis is marked by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the formation of chiasmata?

A scientist observed that 20 out of 100 cells were in prophase, 15 in metaphase, 10 in anaphase, and 5 in telophase. If the total cell cycle time is 10 hours, how many hours do the cells spend in mitosis?
If a cell has 2n = 46 chromosomes, what will be the number of chromosomes in each gamete after meiosis?
Which phase of mitosis is characterised by the alignment of chromosomes at the equator of the cell?
If a cell has a cell cycle of 23 hours and 88 out of 120 cells are in interphase, what is the approximate duration of the mitotic phase?
What is the term used to describe the sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesizes other cell components, and divides into two daughter cells?
What is the term used to describe the sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell, and eventually divides into two daughter cells?
If a cell has 2C DNA content in the G1 phase, what will be its DNA content after the S phase?
Which phase of the cell cycle involves DNA replication?
In which phase of the cell cycle do homologous chromosomes pair up and undergo crossing over?
Which phase of the cell cycle is known as the period of preparation for cell division?
Which phase of the cell cycle is described as the phase between two successive M phases?
What is the main difference between mitosis and meiosis?
What is the result of crossing over during meiosis?
If a cell has 46 chromosomes in its nucleus, how many chromosomes will each daughter cell have after mitosis?
Which phase of meiosis is characterised by the pairing of homologous chromosomes?
In which phase of meiosis do the homologous chromosomes align on the equatorial plate?
What is the role of recombination nodules during meiosis?
